analysis.visual_description: The afternoon house is an ordinary house. He is on the stage. Nothing in his hand names the part he is playing, and he does not name it to himself. The yard is the size a Monday is, and not the size Saturday was.

Kemp gets the laugh on a line that is already in the book. He does not turn, and he does not ask for a line to be written in. The fan of Saturday is not in this play. The laugh spends itself, and the scene goes on.

Between the scenes he is in the tiring-house with the roll he already had. Kemp is in the same air and is not at his elbow. No one is counting a new sum of clowns, and no one is opening a margin to begin one.
